documents.text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines information retrieval with text generation. It retrieves relevant external documents from a knowledge source and provides their content to a language model so that the model can generate more accurate, context-grounded responses.

Hybrid search combines semantic search and keyword-based search. Semantic search uses vector embeddings to find documents based on contextual meaning, while keyword search uses term matching such as BM25. Combining both approaches can improve information retrieval.

Reranking improves retrieval quality by scoring candidate documents against a search query and sorting them by relevance. In a RAG pipeline, a reranker selects the most useful retrieved context before it is passed to the language model.
Database indexing improves database query performance by organizing records for faster lookup. Common index structures include B-trees and hash indexes.
Software testing helps identify defects in applications. Unit tests verify individual components, while integration tests verify interactions between multiple components.
